memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then use it to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the covenant law, the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its accessories, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand. You shall consecrate them so they will be most holy, and whatever touches them will be holy." - Exodus 30:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything gets anointed. Not just the ark and the altar, but the table, the lampstand, the basin, the utensils, the accessories — right down to the smallest tools. Every object involved in serving God was touched with the sacred oil and set apart.

Nothing was considered too minor to be consecrated. The pots and shovels used for ashes received the same setting apart as the ark of the covenant. If it was used in God's service, it was made holy.

That has a striking application to ordinary life. We tend to divide our activities into "spiritual" and "secular" — prayer and Bible reading in one category, working, cooking, commuting, and paying bills in another. But God's pattern here suggests otherwise. Paul says whatever you do, whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God (1 Cor 10:31). The utensils were holy. So is your keyboard, your kitchen, your workbench, your car. Ask God to consecrate the ordinary tools of your daily life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I divide my life into "spiritual" and "ordinary" categories?
What everyday tools or tasks could I deliberately offer to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, nothing used in Your service is too ordinary to be holy. Consecrate the everyday tools and tasks of my life, and help me do all of it for Your glory. Amen.
